rivals.blurb: Soham's clean sweep, and it's a real, named rivalry, not just a scheduling coincidence. Taylor's the better-built roster too (Tier 3 vs Tier 5), so 2026 looks like more of the same unless Soham's rookies hit fast.

The single most lopsided series in the entire league. Six meetings, six losses, and it's not just history: Dev's got the deeper roster too (Tier 3 vs Tier 5). Somewhere out there is a version of Soham that beats Dev. It has never been this one.

Soham's one true house of dominance. Whatever's going wrong against everyone else, it isn't going wrong here. Roster-wise it's close (both Tier 5, both rebuilding), so this stays a fair fight even as Soham holds the all-time edge.

Manas has had Soham's number for years, and the schedule doubles down: they open AND close the regular season against each other. Manas's deeper roster (Tier 3 vs Tier 5) makes it a tough ask for Soham to flip the ledger in 2026.

One of Soham's toughest series, and he draws Shiamak twice. Shiamak's stacked RB room (Tier 2) against Soham's threadbare backfield (Tier 5) says this gap isn't closing without a major roster shakeup.

teams.strength: Lightest RB room in the league by name value, a pile of unproven rookies and committee arms with no proven lead back. A legitimate TE1 in Tucker Kraft is the one real strength on this roster.
teams.notes: Lightest RB room in the league despite the team name, rookie flyers and committee arms, no proven lead back. A legitimate TE1 in Tucker Kraft.

rivals.blurb: A clean sweep, and now it's official on the schedule too, meeting in both Week 3 and the Week 14 rematch. Advaith hasn't found a way past Nihar yet, and Nihar (one of the league's top-projected rosters, \#3 leaguewide in 2026 offense+flex points) isn't walking in as an underdog.
Genuine friends, genuinely competitive series. Roster grades are close too (both Tier 3, edge to Vaibhav on 2026 points), so don't expect this one to settle down anytime soon.
Dead even, and both rosters grade out close as well (both Tier 3). If there's a coin-flip rivalry in this league, it's this one.
Advaith's roughest series among his own named rivals. Shiamak's RB-loaded roster (Tier 2) doesn't make 2026 look any friendlier.

One of the league's two champions against the man carrying the campaign's actual team name this year. Historically Taylor's had the edge; rosters are closer than the record suggests (Tier 3 vs Tier 3).
Dead even across four seasons, and roster-wise it's close too (Tier 3 vs Tier 4, edge Advaith on paper). As tidy a rivalry as this league has.
Advaith owns this series, and the season opens and closes with it. First Indians enter as the deeper roster (Tier 3 vs Tier 4), so the head-to-head edge should hold.

The gap here isn't the record, it's the roster: Alan's the single most valuable team in the league by dynasty value. Advaith's kept it close historically; 2026 is a real test of whether that continues against a stacked roster.

teams.strength: No longer a one-man show at receiver: Jefferson, Collins, and Higgins is a genuine top-to-bottom WR trio, and the tight end room (Njoku, Henry, Likely) is no longer bench-only. RB stays committee-run and QB is a Jayden Daniels bet.
teams.notes: A genuine WR1-WR2-WR3 trio in Jefferson, Collins, and Higgins; a three-deep TE room that's no longer bench-only. RB is a committee; QB is a Jayden Daniels bet.

rivals.blurb: The Advaith gauntlet, still active. Nihar grades as one of the league's highest-projected rosters for 2026 (\#3 leaguewide in projected offense+flex points, Tier 3); on paper, this sweep has real staying power.

Nihar's held his own against the league's most decorated owner, which is more than most can say. Alan's roster carries the most dynasty value and the highest 2026 projection in the league, so this stays the toughest measuring stick on Nihar's schedule.

Nihar leads the regular season (Reg 3-2) but Manas flips it in the playoffs, a clean 2-0, including the 2025 semifinal upset (139.00-120.56). Two of the league's most talented 2026 rosters, both Tier 3.
Nihar's most dominant series among his named rivals. Nothing about Achal's rebuilding roster changes that trend heading into 2026.
Dead even, and it opens and closes the year. Nihar's the deeper roster on paper (Tier 3 vs Tier 4), though Dhiraj's genuine rookie RB1 in Jeremiyah Love makes this closer than the tier gap suggests.
Another clean sweep for Nihar, and Varun draws him twice. The roster gap (Tier 3 vs Tier 4) says this one isn't walking through the door in 2026.

teams.strength: A genuinely two-deep backfield now, Bijan Robinson and Kyren Williams are both true starting-caliber backs, plus four viable starting wideouts. The QB room is four capable arms (Murray, Lawrence, Stafford, Prescott) with no true difference-maker.
teams.notes: Two true starting-caliber RBs (Bijan Robinson, Kyren Williams) plus legit starting WRs (Olave, Wilson, London); QB is four capable arms, no true difference-maker.

rivals.blurb: Dev's handled Shiamak more often than not, but Shiamak's the deeper 2026 roster on paper (Tier 2 vs Tier 3). Two shots at flipping the script, in Week 1 and Week 12.

Dev owns the regular season (Reg 4-1) but Achal's 2-0 when the playoffs hit, a real reversal. Dev's the better-built roster on paper for 2026 (Tier 3 vs Tier 5), but this series plays two different ways.
The toughest test on Dev's schedule. Alan's roster carries the most dynasty value in the league; this is as close to an uphill climb as it gets.
Dev's handled his fellow rebuild-mode friend well. Roster grades are close (Tier 3 vs Tier 4), so the history's earned, not gifted.
The most lopsided series in the entire league, and it's a real, named rivalry on top of the history. Dev's also the deeper roster (Tier 3 vs Tier 5). Nothing on paper says 2026 breaks the streak.
Dev's quietly dominant here too. Taylor's the better-graded roster for 2026 (Tier 3 vs Tier 3, edge Taylor on points), so this one's worth an early-season watch.

teams.strength: Bell-cow production at WR1 (Nacua) and RB1 (Achane) sets a strong floor. QB is a three-way youth bet (Maye/Stroud/Purdy) and WR depth is thin behind the top name.
teams.notes: True bell-cows at WR1 (Nacua) and RB1 (Achane); QB is a three-way youth bet (Maye/Stroud/Purdy); WR depth is thin behind Nacua.

rivals.blurb: One of Alan's most one-sided series, and the most valuable roster in the league, by a wide margin, doesn't make it easier on Achal in 2026.
Close on paper, and Alan's the far deeper roster by dynasty value. First Indians will need more than history to flip this one.

The record says close, 3-2, but the rosters don't: Alan's the league's clear Tier 1, Dev's fighting through a crowded Tier 3. Historically, Dev's one of the few who's actually made a series out of it against him.

The league's most decorated owner against its \#3-projected roster for 2026. Alan's still got the historical edge, but this is the closest thing to a true title-defense measuring stick on his schedule.
The league's only two champions, and Alan's dominated the head-to-head anyway. Doesn't matter much on paper either: Alan's roster carries nearly double Taylor's dynasty value.
A clean sweep against one of the league's best-built 2026 rosters (Tier 2). If Shiamak's going to break through this year, this is the series to watch.

teams.strength: Great starters, incredible depth, mixed team age and injury risk.
teams.notes: Elite and deep at WR (six rostered with real value) and TE; RB is by committee but strong. The single most valuable roster in the league.

rivals.blurb: Advaith's had the edge, and the deeper roster too, though not by much (Tier 3 vs Tier 4). Two cracks at it, Week 1 and Week 12.
A clean sweep against one of the league's highest-projected rosters for 2026 (\#3 leaguewide). This is Varun's toughest matchup on paper and on the scoreboard.
Another sweep, and Manas's roster (Tier 3) outgrades Varun's (Tier 4) heading into the year. An uphill closing stretch.
A real rivalry between two rebuilding rosters that grade out close (Tier 4 vs Tier 3). Whoever wins this one probably needs it more.
Dead even across four seasons. Vaibhav's the deeper roster on paper now (Tier 3 vs Tier 4), so 2026 is a real test of whether the series stays even.
The closest thing to a fair fight on Varun's whole schedule; roster grades are close too (Tier 4 vs Tier 5), and neither's clearly ahead on paper either.

teams.strength: A legitimate RB1 in Breece Hall plus a genuinely deep WR room (Metcalf, Pickens, Flowers, Dell, Concepcion, Shaheed), with Mahomes anchoring QB.
teams.notes: A real RB1 (Hall) plus a deep WR room (Metcalf/Pickens/Flowers/Dell/Concepcion/Shaheed), with Mahomes still an elite, low-risk anchor at QB.

rivals.blurb: The single hardest matchup on Achal's calendar, against the league's most valuable roster, twice.

On paper and in the regular season, this is Dev's series (Reg 1-4 for Achal). The playoffs flip it clean, Achal's 2-0 there. Rosters aren't as close as the head-to-head suggests (Tier 5 vs Tier 3), so don't judge this one by the regular season alone.
Achal's actually got the head-to-head edge here, even though Vaibhav's the far deeper 2026 roster (Tier 3 vs Tier 5). Worth watching for an upset.
Achal's roughest series among his named rivals, and Nihar grades as one of the league's top rosters this year (\#3 in projected points). No relief in sight on paper.
One of the few series Achal's actually trailing by a lot. Roster grades are close (both Tier 5, both rebuilding), so this one's earned, not systemic.
A real toss-up between two similarly-built rosters. Neither side's pulled away, and nothing on paper says 2026 changes that.

teams.strength: Two real intriguing pieces now, an established WR1 in McConkey and a rookie with real juice in Makai Lemon, but the QB room (Watson/Willis/Penix/Cousins) and a crowded, lead-back-less RB committee still cap the ceiling.
teams.notes: Two real difference-making pieces in McConkey and rookie Makai Lemon; the RB room (Wright/Coleman/Bigsby/Monangai/Holani/Pollard) is a deep committee with no clear lead, and QB remains unsettled.

rivals.blurb: A real, named rivalry that's also a season-opening-and-closing double matchup. Manas has struggled here despite the stronger roster on paper (Tier 3 vs Tier 4), and Dhiraj's genuine rookie RB1 in Jeremiyah Love only narrows that gap further.
Dead even, and roster grades are close (both Tier 3). A genuine coin flip.

The regular season says Nihar (Reg 2-3 for Manas), the playoffs say Manas, a clean 2-0 that ended Nihar's best-ever season in the 2025 semifinal. Two of the league's best-built 2026 rosters, and maybe the title decider.

Manas's most dominant series among his named rivals, even against a Tier 3 peer with the higher dynasty value on paper (edge Manas on 2026 projected points, edge Vaibhav on dynasty value). History's clearly on Manas's side here.
Manas has had the edge, and the deeper roster too (Tier 3 vs Tier 5). Opens and closes the season.
A clean sweep, and Manas's roster clearly outgrades Varun's for 2026 (Tier 3 vs Tier 4). Two more shots to extend it.

teams.strength: Elite top end at WR and TE, including a rare two-deep young tight end room. QB is the soft spot (Bryce Young/Sam Darnold, no proven veteran arm), and RB is still a committee with no clear lead back.
teams.notes: Elite WR1 in Smith-Njigba; a two-deep young-TE room (Bowers + Loveland) nobody else in the league has. QB downgraded to Young/Darnold; RB is a committee with no lead back.

rivals.blurb: A real, named rivalry and a double matchup in the same season. Tier 2 vs Tier 3, arguably one of the closest fair fights in the whole league.
One of Shiamak's most dominant series. The roster gap (Tier 2 vs Tier 4) is real on paper too.
Shiamak's owned this one, and enters 2026 as the clearly deeper roster (Tier 2 vs Tier 3).
Shiamak's one true bad matchup among his named rivals, against the league's most valuable roster. If 2026 is Shiamak's breakout year, this is the series that needs to flip.
Dev's had the edge, but Shiamak's the deeper 2026 roster (Tier 2 vs Tier 3). A good early bounce-back opportunity, twice.
Shiamak's handled this one comfortably, and the roster gap (Tier 2 vs Tier 5) says that continues into 2026.

teams.strength: Amazing starters in key positions, shallow depth, mixed to older team age and high injury risk.
teams.notes: RB monopoly, Gibbs, Taylor, and McCaffrey are three top-15 backs on one roster; a true WR1 in Egbuka; a rushing-QB anchor.

rivals.blurb: A real rivalry and a double matchup in one, between a Tier 2 and Tier 3 roster. Arguably one of the more evenly matched series on the whole schedule.
Genuinely close, genuinely competitive. Vaibhav's the deeper roster on paper now, so 2026 is a real chance to flip the series.
Dhiraj's had the edge here, though the roster picture favors Vaibhav clearly on paper.
Dead even across four seasons, and Vaibhav's now the deeper roster (Tier 3 vs Tier 4). 2026 is a real test of whether the tie holds.
Vaibhav's roughest series among his named rivals, against one of the league's better-built 2026 rosters. Room to grow here.
Taylor's had the edge, though the roster grades are close now too (both Tier 3). Opens and closes the year.
Vaibhav's actually trailing this one on the scoreboard despite the far stronger roster (Tier 3 vs Tier 5). An upset-watch matchup either way.

teams.strength: Elite young RB duo in Jeanty and Hampton, plus a genuinely deep WR room (Amon-Ra St. Brown, McMillan, Travis Hunter, Odunze, Shakir).
teams.notes: Elite young RB duo (Jeanty + Hampton); deep WR room (St. Brown/McMillan/Hunter/Odunze/Shakir).

rivals.blurb: A clean sweep and a real, named rivalry, doubled up on the schedule too. Taylor's also the better-graded roster (Tier 3 vs Tier 5).
The league's only two champions, and Alan's owned the head-to-head. Alan's roster also carries nearly double Taylor's dynasty value: this is the toughest fight on Taylor's whole schedule.
Taylor's had the better of this one, against a First Indians roster that grades out close (Tier 3 vs Tier 3).
One of the few series Taylor's actually trailing. Roster grades are close (Tier 3 vs Tier 3), so this one's a fair fight worth watching.
Taylor's had the edge, though the rosters grade out close now too (both Tier 3). Two shots to defend it.
Taylor's most dominant series, full stop, and the roster picture (Tier 3 vs Tier 4) doesn't obviously change that.

teams.strength: Deeper than the record suggests. Lamb and Allen are true superstars, and both WR (Golden/Pittman/Rice/Evans/Hill/Samuel) and RB (Jacobs/Barkley/Ekeler/White) go far further down the roster than most Tier 3 teams.
teams.notes: Two true superstars (Lamb, Allen); real depth at both WR (six-plus rostered names) and RB (Jacobs/Barkley/White) that goes further than most of this tier.

rivals.blurb: A real, named rivalry doubled up on the schedule, and Dhiraj's dominated it despite Manas grading as the deeper roster on paper (Tier 3 vs Tier 4).
Dhiraj's held the edge here, even though Vaibhav grades as the deeper roster on paper (Tier 3 vs Tier 4).
One of Dhiraj's roughest series, against a Tier 2 roster. Room to grow in 2026.
Dead even across four seasons against the man carrying the campaign's actual team name. As tidy a rivalry as this league has.
Dead even, against one of the league's top-projected 2026 rosters (\#3 leaguewide). Two shots to take the lead, in Week 1 and Week 12.
Dhiraj's toughest series by far, against one of the league's two all-time champions. Two more cracks at it to close the season.

teams.strength: A real rookie RB1 in Jeremiyah Love, paired with the Nabers/Smith/Tate WR trio, gives this roster a legitimate starting core, even if the record hasn't caught up yet.
teams.notes: A true WR1-WR2-WR3 in Nabers, Smith, and Tate, now paired with a genuine rookie RB1 in Jeremiyah Love. This is a deeper roster than its record shows.

history.note: Alan snuck in at 7-7, upset Achal's league-best 11-3 squad in the semifinal, then beat Dhiraj for the ring.
Alan, Nihar and Taylor tied for the best record at 10-4. Taylor blew out Alan in the final.
Alan went wire to wire: 12-2, then the largest championship margin on record (65.78). Achal cratered to 1-13.
Nihar posted the best record at 12-2, but Manas knocked him out in the semifinal, 139.00–120.56, before losing the final to Alan.
